```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Two expected rxode2 notes are muffled, and only these two: the
# occasion-indexed between-occasion etas cannot be mu-referenced (rxode2 says
# so each time it builds the model), and typical-value solves of several
# subjects run without omega on purpose.
quiet_rx <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("non-mu referenced|without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}
mod <- quiet_rx(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Calderin_2026_sorfequiline")))
mod_typ <- quiet_rx(rxode2::zeroRe(mod))
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70331> (open access; Supporting
  Information Section S1 holds the NONMEM control stream of the final model)

Sorfequiline (TBAJ-876) is a diarylquinoline in development for
tuberculosis. Its major metabolite, M3, is pharmacologically active. The model
describes both analytes jointly, with a fraction of the absorbed dose (FAM)
appearing directly as M3 to represent first-pass metabolism in the gut wall.

# Population

The model was fitted to `r mod$population$n_subjects`
healthy adult volunteers pooled from two phase 1 studies run in the United
States (Calderin 2026 Table 1): CL-001 (NCT04493671; a single-ascending-dose
part with 10-800 mg oral suspension fasted plus 100 mg fed, n = 55; a
multiple-ascending-dose part with 25, 75 or 200 mg once daily for 14 days fed,
n = 27; and a relative-bioavailability part with a 100 mg tablet fed or fasted
or 4 x 25 mg tablets fasted, n = 30) and CL-002 (NCT05526911; a
drug-drug-interaction study with 200 mg once daily then 165 mg suspension fed,
n = 26). Median age was 35 years (19-55), median weight 77 kg (49-153) and
median fat-free mass 53 kg (33-82); 52% were female, 57% White and 38% Black
or African American, and 51% Hispanic or Latino. 4638 samples were analysed;
4.0% of sorfequiline and 17.0% of M3 concentrations were below the 1 ng/mL
limit of quantification.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Calderin_2026_sorfequiline")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value in `ini()` was checked against both Table 2 and the NONMEM control
stream of Supporting Information Section S1; the two agree for every
estimate. In-file comments in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Calderin_2026_sorfequiline.R` give the same
locations.

# Replicating Figure 2: summed AUC0-24 over 12 weeks

Figure 2 of the paper shows the summed daily exposure
AUC0-24,sum = AUC0-24,sorfequiline + AUC0-24,M3 over 12 weeks of once-daily
tablet dosing with food at 25, 50 and 100 mg, either without a loading phase
or with two weeks at 2, 3 or 4 times the maintenance dose. The simulated
individual has the cohort's typical fat-free mass (53 kg). As in the paper,
the CL-002 bioavailability effect and the high-dose effect are switched off.

```{r fig2-events}
regimens <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  maint = c(25, 50, 100),
  load_factor = c(1, 2, 3, 4)
) |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    loading = ifelse(load_factor == 1, "No loading dose",
                     paste0(load_factor, "x maintenance dose")),
    regimen = paste0(maint, " mg, ", loading)
  )

make_events <- function(reg, obs_step = 1) {
  doses <- reg |>
    tidyr::crossing(day = 0:83) |>
    mutate(
      time = day * 24,
      amt = ifelse(day < 14, maint * load_factor, maint),
      evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- reg |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 84 * 24, by = obs_step)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, maint, load_factor, regimen) |>
    mutate(FFM = 53, FED = 1, FORM_TABLET = 1, STUDY_CL002 = 0,
           DOSE_HIGH = 0, OCC = 1) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_typ <- make_events(regimens)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_typ[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r fig2-simulate}
sim_typ <- quiet_rx(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, events_typ,
  keep = c("maint", "load_factor", "regimen"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)) |>
  mutate(Csum = Cc + Cc_m3)
```

The daily AUC0-24 of the summed concentration is computed with PKNCA, one
interval per dosing day.

```{r fig2-pknca}
conc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Csum)) |>
  select(id, time, Csum, regimen)
dose_typ <- events_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)

intervals_daily <- data.frame(
  start = (0:83) * 24,
  end = (1:84) * 24,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Csum ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = intervals_daily
))
auc_daily <- as.data.frame(nca_typ$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(day = end / 24, week = end / 24 / 7) |>
  left_join(regimens |> select(regimen, maint, loading), by = "regimen")
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(auc_daily, aes(week, PPORRES, linetype = loading)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 62.2, linetype = "dashed", colour = "orange") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 127.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(maint, "mg"), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "AUC0-24,sum (mg*h/L)", linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2 of Calderin 2026 (typical individual,",
                       "FFM 53 kg, tablet with food). Dashed lines: NOAEL 62.2",
                       "and LOAEL 127.5 mg*h/L.")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Comparison against Figure 2

The published lines were digitised by the maintainers from Figure 2, with the
vertical axis calibrated on its tick labels (the LOAEL line reads back as
127.8 against the printed 127.5 mg*h/L). Only points where each line can be
told apart are used; after the loading phase the 25 mg lines and several of
the 50 and 100 mg lines overlap. A point at week *w* is compared with the
AUC0-24 of the dosing day that ends at day round(7*w).

```{r fig2-compare}
published_fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~maint, ~load_factor, ~week, ~auc_fig,
  100, 4, 1.0, 26.2,
  100, 3, 1.0, 19.8,
  100, 2, 1.0, 13.1,
  100, 1, 1.0,  6.7,
  100, 4, 1.9, 29.7,
  100, 3, 1.9, 22.3,
  100, 1, 1.9,  7.4,
  100, 4, 4.0, 13.8,
  100, 3, 4.0, 12.2,
  100, 2, 4.0, 10.6,
  100, 1, 4.0,  9.0,
  100, 4, 11.9, 16.3,
   50, 4, 1.0, 13.3,
   50, 3, 1.0,  9.7,
   50, 2, 1.0,  6.7,
   50, 1, 1.0,  3.2,
   50, 4, 1.9, 14.7,
   50, 3, 1.9, 11.0,
   50, 2, 1.9,  7.4,
   50, 1, 1.9,  3.7,
   25, 4, 1.0,  6.4,
   25, 3, 1.0,  4.8,
   25, 2, 1.0,  3.2,
   25, 1, 1.0,  1.6,
   25, 1, 11.9, 3.4
) |>
  mutate(day = round(7 * week))

fig2_cmp <- published_fig2 |>
  left_join(regimens |> select(maint, load_factor, regimen),
            by = c("maint", "load_factor")) |>
  left_join(auc_daily |> select(regimen, day, auc_sim = PPORRES),
            by = c("regimen", "day")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_fig) / auc_fig)

fig2_cmp |>
  select(regimen, week, auc_fig, auc_sim, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Week" = week,
    "Figure 2 (mg*h/L)" = auc_fig,
    "Simulated (mg*h/L)" = auc_sim,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "Typical-value AUC0-24,sum against Figure 2 of Calderin 2026.")

# Deterministic typical-value solve against a digitised figure: the residual
# difference is digitisation error (about 0.5 mg*h/L at this resolution) plus
# the gap between a typical value and the paper's median of 500 stochastic
# replicates.
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig2_cmp) == nrow(published_fig2),
  !anyNA(fig2_cmp$auc_sim),
  abs(median(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)) < 5,
  all(abs(fig2_cmp$pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

All digitised points are reproduced within
`r round(max(abs(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)), 1)`% (median difference
`r round(median(fig2_cmp$pct_diff), 1)`%), and the model reproduces the
paper's conclusion that the typical summed exposure stays well below the
NOAEL of 62.2 mg*h/L in every regimen.

## Variability band for the 4x loading regimens

Figure 2 also shades the 90% prediction interval of the 4x-loading regimens.
The chunk below simulates 200 replicates of the typical individual per
maintenance dose with between-subject and between-occasion variability. All
doses are assigned to occasion 1, so each replicate carries one draw of the
occasion effects for the whole course (see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r fig2-band}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261117)
reg_4x <- regimens |> filter(load_factor == 4)
events_var <- reg_4x |>
  select(maint, load_factor, regimen) |>
  tidyr::crossing(rep = 1:200) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n())) |>
  select(-rep) |>
  make_events(obs_step = 2)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_var[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_var <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events_var, keep = c("maint", "regimen"),
                           returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(Csum = Cc + Cc_m3)

# Daily trapezoidal AUC on the 2-h grid (pure numerical integration of the
# simulated profile; the PKNCA calculation above is the validation).
auc_var <- sim_var |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  group_by(id, maint) |>
  mutate(seg = (time - lag(time)) * (Csum + lag(Csum)) / 2,
         day = ceiling(time / 24)) |>
  filter(day >= 1) |>
  group_by(id, maint, day) |>
  summarise(auc = sum(seg), .groups = "drop")

band <- auc_var |>
  group_by(maint, day) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(auc, 0.05), med = median(auc),
            hi = quantile(auc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(band, aes(day / 7)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(maint, "mg"), nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "AUC0-24,sum (mg*h/L)",
       caption = "4x maintenance loading for 2 weeks: median and 90% interval of 200 replicates.") +
  theme_bw()

band_wk2 <- band |> filter(day == 13)
knitr::kable(band_wk2, digits = 1,
             caption = "Day-13 summed AUC0-24 (mg*h/L), 4x loading regimens.")

# The median of the stochastic replicates should sit near the digitised
# Figure 2 line (which is itself such a median); the band is wide, so the
# check is on the centre only.
med_100 <- band_wk2$med[band_wk2$maint == 100]
stopifnot(abs(med_100 - 29.7) / 29.7 < 0.25)
```

The simulated median at the end of loading
(`r round(med_100, 1)` mg*h/L for 100 mg) agrees with the Figure 2 line, but the
simulated 90% interval
(`r round(band_wk2$lo[band_wk2$maint == 100], 1)` to
`r round(band_wk2$hi[band_wk2$maint == 100], 1)` mg*h/L) is wider than the
published band, which spans roughly 20 to 50 mg*h/L. Holding one draw of the
between-occasion effects on F, ka and MTT for the whole course makes the
53% occasion variability on F behave like between-subject variability; if
the paper drew a fresh occasion effect for each dose, those effects average
out over the daily doses and the band narrows. The paper does not state which
it did, so the band is shown for illustration and is not used as a gate.

# Single-dose profiles: the food effect on first-pass M3

The fraction of the absorbed dose that enters the circulation as M3 falls from
0.464 fasted to 0.157 fed. A single 100 mg suspension dose illustrates the
shift in the parent / metabolite balance.

```{r single-dose}
sd_events <- tibble(id = 1:2, FED = c(0, 1)) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, seq(0.25, 168, by = 0.25))) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(id = 1:2, FED = c(0, 1), time = 0, amt = 100,
                   evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)) |>
  mutate(FFM = 53, FORM_TABLET = 0, STUDY_CL002 = 0, DOSE_HIGH = 0, OCC = 1,
         treatment = ifelse(FED == 1, "100 mg fed", "100 mg fasted")) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sd_sim <- quiet_rx(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, sd_events,
                                   keep = c("treatment"),
                                   returnType = "data.frame"))

sd_sim |>
  select(time, treatment, Sorfequiline = Cc, M3 = Cc_m3) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Sorfequiline, M3), names_to = "analyte",
                      values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc * 1000, colour = analyte, linetype = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Typical individual, 100 mg oral suspension.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA by analyte and food status

```{r single-dose-pknca}
sd_doses <- sd_events |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment)
sd_int <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                     auclast = TRUE)

nca_one <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- sd_sim |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    select(id, time, treatment, conc = all_of(conc_col))
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(sd_doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = sd_int
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    mutate(analyte = conc_col)
}
sd_nca <- bind_rows(nca_one("Cc"), nca_one("Cc_m3")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

sd_nca |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc", "Sorfequiline", "M3"),
         cmax = cmax * 1000) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Analyte" = analyte,
    "Treatment" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-168 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical single-dose NCA (no published NCA to compare).")

# Food moves exposure from M3 towards the parent: the M3 / parent AUC ratio
# must fall with food, a structural consequence of FAM 0.464 -> 0.157.
ratio <- sd_nca |>
  select(treatment, analyte, auclast) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, values_from = auclast) |>
  mutate(ratio = Cc_m3 / Cc)
stopifnot(ratio$ratio[ratio$treatment == "100 mg fed"] <
            0.7 * ratio$ratio[ratio$treatment == "100 mg fasted"])
```

The paper does not report NCA values, so the table above has no published
comparator. Its purpose is to show the food effect the model encodes: fed
dosing raises sorfequiline exposure (faster absorption and less first-pass
loss to M3) and lowers the M3 / sorfequiline exposure ratio.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual-error correlation not encoded.** The paper correlates the
  sorfequiline and M3 residual errors (rho = 0.786, Table 2, implemented with
  the NONMEM L2 data item). nlmixr2 residual-error models are independent per
  endpoint, so the two endpoints here have independent combined additive +
  proportional errors with the published magnitudes. Typical-value and
  between-subject predictions are unaffected; simulated observations of the
  two analytes from the same sample will be less correlated than in the
  source data.
- **BLQ handling.** The M7+ method (BLQ imputed as zero with the additive
  error inflated by the LLOQ) is an estimation device and is not part of the
  packaged model. The additive error is the `THETA(12) = 0 FIX` plus
  0.2 x LLOQ = 0.0002 mg/L of the control stream.
- **Number of transit compartments.** Table 2 lists "NN = 3 Fixed"; the control
  stream sets `THETA(10) = 2 FIX` and `KTR = (NN+1)/MTT`, with three explicit
  transit compartments before the absorption compartment. Both describe the
  same structure: three transfers at ktr = 3 / MTT (depot -> transit1 ->
  transit2 -> transit3), then ka out of the absorption compartment
  (`transit3` here). The control stream's form is used.
- **Units.** The control stream tracks amounts in moles (F1 = BIO / (657.55 x
  1000)) and converts back to mg/L with each analyte's molecular weight. The
  packaged model tracks mg and converts parent mass to M3 mass with the factor
  643.55 / 657.55 at formation; the two are the same model.
- **Between-occasion variability.** Implemented with three occasion slots
  selected by `OCC`, exactly as the control stream does; records outside
  occasions 1-3 receive no BOV. The paper defines an occasion as a dosing event
  and its subsequent observations but does not say how occasions were numbered
  in the multiple-dose parts. The control stream also declares a BOV on CL with
  variance 0 FIX and zero-variance BSV on all other disposition parameters,
  ka, F and MTT; these are omitted.
- **Variability band in Figure 2.** The paper simulated 500 replicates of the
  typical individual; how the BOV was assigned across 84 daily doses is not
  stated. This vignette assigns all doses to occasion 1 (one BOV draw per
  replicate), and the resulting 90% band is wider than the published one. The
  digitised comparison uses the typical-value solve.
- **High-dose and CL-002 effects.** `DOSE_HIGH` (400 and 800 mg) and
  `STUDY_CL002` are included as estimated, but the paper did not apply either
  in its regimen simulations; both are 0 in all simulations here.
- **Values not from the paper's text or tables.** The Figure 2 comparison
  points were digitised by the maintainers from Figure 2. Every model
  parameter comes from Table 2 and the control stream.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article as of 2026-11-17.
